questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml:
The Cost Price of an item is Y. The shopkeeper marked it up by 50%. He then offers two successive discounts of X% and 10%. The total discount amount is 420. Y/10 is a perfect square, Y is a four-digit number less than 1500, and X is an integer.

Statements:
I. X = 20%.
II. Selling Price = ₹1080.
III. Marked Price − Cost Price = ₹720.

options.text: Both I and III are false

solution.summary: The only admissible value is Y = 1000, giving X = 20% and SP = ₹1080. Statement III is false.

steps.title: 1. List possible Y
steps.bodyHtml: Since Y/10 is a perfect square and Y is between 1000 and 1499, Y can only be 1000, 1210 or 1440.

steps.title: 2. Use the discount equation
steps.bodyHtml: Marked Price = 1.5Y. Selling Price = 1.5Y × (1 − X/100) × 0.9. Also, MP − SP = 420.

steps.title: 3. Test the three Y values
steps.bodyHtml: For Y = 1000, SP = 1500 − 420 = 1080. Hence 1080 = 1350(1 − X/100), so X = 20%. For Y = 1210 and 1440, X is not an integer.

steps.title: 4. Check statements
steps.bodyHtml: I is true and II is true. But MP − CP = 1500 − 1000 = 500, not 720. So III is false.

solution.quickMethod: Try the very small set Y = 1000, 1210, 1440 first; the integer-X condition immediately fixes Y = 1000.
solution.trap: Do not treat successive discounts as X% + 10%.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml: A positive integer k satisfies 20k−19 + 21k−19 = 29k−19. The series is k, (k+12), (k+36), (k+84), P. Find P.

solution.summary: The exponent k−19 must be 2, so k = 21. The series differences double each time; hence P = 201.

steps.title: 1. Find k
steps.bodyHtml: Let n = k − 19. Then 20<sup>n</sup> + 21<sup>n</sup> = 29<sup>n</sup>. For n = 2, 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841 = 29². The positive-integer solution is therefore n = 2, so k = 21.

steps.title: 2. Continue the series
steps.bodyHtml: 21, 33, 57, 105, P. Differences are 12, 24, 48, so the next difference is 96.

solution.quickMethod: Notice 20² + 21² = 29² immediately; this is the key to fixing k.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml: A merchant buys cloth at ₹100 per metre and gets 5 cm free for every 100 cm purchased. He sells at ₹110 per metre but gives only 95 cm for every 100 cm charged. If he gives a 5% discount, what is his profit percentage?

solution.summary: He effectively pays ₹100 for 105 cm but receives ₹104.50 for only 95 cm sold. Converting both to the same 105 cm basis gives a 15.5% profit.

steps.title: 1. Effective cost
steps.bodyHtml: ₹100 buys 100 cm + 5 cm free = 105 cm. So cost of 105 cm = ₹100.

steps.title: 2. Effective selling price
steps.bodyHtml: After 5% discount, ₹110 becomes ₹104.50 for the 95 cm actually supplied per billed metre.

steps.title: 3. Put both on the 105 cm basis

solution.quickMethod: Combine both cheats into one ratio: effective revenue = 110 × 95% × 105/95 = 115.5 against cost 100.
solution.trap: Discount is applied to the billed selling rate; the 95 cm cheating ratio must also be included.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml: Given x<sup>2</sup> + (p−2)x + (q+2) = 0, the sum of its coefficients and constant term is 11. If p and q are positive integers with p > q and the roots are real, let n be the number of possible (p,q) pairs. Find n<sup>2</sup> + 5.

solution.summary: The coefficient condition gives p+q=10. Exactly three positive pairs satisfy the real-root condition, so n=3 and n²+5=14.

steps.title: 2. List p>q pairs
steps.bodyHtml: Possible pairs are (6,4), (7,3), (8,2), (9,1).

steps.title: 3. Apply the discriminant
steps.bodyHtml: Δ = (p−2)² − 4(q+2) ≥ 0. The pair (6,4) fails; (7,3), (8,2) and (9,1) work. Hence n=3.

solution.trap: The phrase ‘sum of the coefficients and constant term’ includes the coefficient of x², i.e. 1.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml:
Two articles A and B are bought at the same cost price. A is sold at a profit of R1%. B is marked up by M% and then sold at 10% discount. The markup M and B's profit% are roots of x2 − 37.5x + 312.5 = 0. In y2 − 35y + K = 0, the roots differ by 5 and the larger root is R1. Total profit on both articles is ₹260. Which statements are true?

I. CP of each article is ₹850.
II. SP of A is ₹960.
III. M = 20%.

options.text: Both I and II are true

solution.summary: M and B's profit% are 25% and 12.5%; R1 is 20%. This gives CP ₹800 and SP of A ₹960. Only II is true.

steps.title: 1. Solve the first quadratic
steps.bodyHtml: Roots of x²−37.5x+312.5 are 25 and 12.5. Thus M=25% and B's profit=12.5%.

steps.title: 2. Find R1
steps.bodyHtml: The second quadratic has sum of roots 35 and difference 5. Hence roots are 20 and 15; the larger root is R1, so R1=20%.

steps.title: 3. Find the common cost price
steps.bodyHtml: Total profit = 20% of CP + 12.5% of CP = 32.5% of CP = 260. Therefore CP = ₹800.

steps.title: 4. Check statements
steps.bodyHtml: SP(A)=800×1.20=₹960, so II is true. I says ₹850, false. III says M=20%, but M=25%, false.

solution.quickMethod: For two numbers with sum 35 and difference 5, roots are 20 and 15 instantly.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml: Equation I: (x<sup>2</sup> − 13x + 40)<sup>6</sup> ≤ 0. Equation II: (y<sup>2</sup> − 19y + 84)<sup>7</sup> ≤ 0. Find the relationship between x and y.

options.text: x = y or relationship cannot be established

solution.summary: Equation I forces x to be 5 or 8, while Equation II allows every y from 7 to 12. Therefore no single relation between x and y holds.

steps.title: 1. Solve Equation I
steps.bodyHtml: An even power is never negative. For the expression to be ≤0, the base must be 0: x²−13x+40=0 ⇒ (x−5)(x−8)=0. So x=5 or 8.

steps.title: 2. Solve Equation II
steps.bodyHtml: An odd power preserves the sign, so y²−19y+84≤0 ⇒ (y−7)(y−12)≤0. Hence 7≤y≤12.

steps.title: 3. Compare
steps.bodyHtml: If x=5, then x<y. If x=8, y may be 7, 8, 9, …, 12. So x<y, x=y and x>y are all possible across the allowed values. A fixed relationship cannot be established.

solution.trap: The even power and odd power behave differently with inequalities.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml:
P is invested at R% SI for 3 years and the same P at (R+10)% CI for 2 years. The difference in interests is ₹1215. P is a four-digit multiple of 125, R is a prime less than 7, and P/R = 3125. Which statements are true?

I. At (R+3)% SI for 5 years, interest is ₹1562.5.
II. CI interest is ₹1590.
III. P is 250% of ₹2500.

options.text: Both I and II are true
Both II and III are true
All I, II, and III are true

solution.summary: R=2 and P=6250 satisfy all conditions. Every statement then checks out.

steps.title: 1. Use P/R = 3125
steps.bodyHtml: R is prime and less than 7, so R∈{2,3,5}. Since P=3125R must be four-digit, R can be 2 or 3. Thus P is 6250 or 9375.

steps.title: 4. Check II and III
steps.bodyHtml: CI interest is ₹1590. Also 6250 = 2.5×2500 = 250% of 2500. All three statements are true.

solution.finalAnswer: E — All I, II, and III are true

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml:
M and (M+2000) are invested. M earns X% SI for 3 years; (M+2000) earns 20% CI for 2 years. Total interest is ₹13880. M/500 and X are consecutive multiples of 5, with M/500 > X. Which statements are true?

I. M is a multiple of 2500.
II. X = 25%.
III. Difference between the two interests is ₹1120.

options.text: Both I and II are false

solution.summary: The consecutive multiples are M/500 = 25 and X = 20, giving M = ₹12500. So I and III are true; II is false.

steps.title: 3. Use the consecutive-multiple condition
steps.bodyHtml: m and X are consecutive multiples of 5 with m>X. The valid pair is m=25, X=20. Hence M=25×500=₹12500.

steps.title: 4. Check statements
steps.bodyHtml: ₹12500 is a multiple of ₹2500, so I is true. X=20%, so II is false. SI=₹7500 and CI=₹6380; the difference is ₹1120, so III is true.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml: On Day 2, the processing rate for the first 4 hours of the 2nd Interval was 20 MT/hr. What was the processing rate for the remaining hours of that same interval?

solution.summary: Each interval is 6 hours. Day 2 Interval 2 has 150 MT; 80 MT was processed in the first 4 hours, leaving 70 MT over 2 hours = 35 MT/hr.

steps.title: 2. Find remaining cargo
steps.bodyHtml: Total in Day 2 Interval 2 = 150 MT. First 4 hours at 20 MT/hr gives 4×20=80 MT. Remaining = 150−80=70 MT.

steps.title: 3. Compute remaining rate
steps.bodyHtml: Remaining time = 6−4=2 hours. Rate = 70/2 = 35 MT/hr.

questions.questionHtml: What is the difference between the cargo processed in the 1st Interval of Day 4 and the 4th Interval of Day 3?

solution.summary: Day 4 Interval 1 = 160 MT and Day 3 Interval 4 = 50 MT, so the difference is 110 MT.

steps.title: 1. Read both values
steps.bodyHtml: Day 4 I1 = 160 MT. Day 3 I4 = 50 MT.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml: If fuel consumption is 2 units per MT processed, what is the total fuel consumed during the 4th Interval on Day 1 and Day 5 combined?

solution.summary: Day 1 I4 = 40 MT and Day 5 I4 = 100 MT, so 140 MT is processed. At 2 units/MT, fuel = 280 units.

questions.subject: quants
questions.questionHtml:
Determine the truth status of the following statements:
I. Day 2 Interval 3 is exactly 25% more than Day 5 Interval 2.
II. The average of Day 1, Day 3 and Day 5 Interval 4 values is 63.33 MT.
III. The difference between the highest and lowest cargo values on Day 4 is 80 MT.

solution.summary: I is false because both values are 140. II is true because 190/3 = 63.33 MT. III is true because Day 4 ranges from 160 to 240 MT.

steps.title: 1. Check Statement I
steps.bodyHtml: Day 2 I3 = 140 and Day 5 I2 = 140. So X=Y, not X=1.25Y. False.

steps.title: 3. Check Statement III
steps.bodyHtml: Day 4 values are 160, 200, 200, 240. Difference = 240−160 = 80 MT. True.

solution.finalAnswer: B — I False, II True, III True
